record.context_brief: CPSD-rank of the average mixing matrix
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with average mixing matrix \hat{M}=lim_{T→∞}(1/T)∫_0^T M(t)dt = Σ_r E_r∘E_r. The completely positive semidefinite rank (cpsd-rank) of \hat{M} is the smallest matrix dimension d for which \hat{M} can be realized as a Gram matrix of positive semidefinite d×d matrices. Compute the cpsd-rank of \hat{M}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A$, and let $A=\sum_{r=0}^{d} \lambda_r E_r$ be its spectral decomposition, where the $E_r$ are the orthogonal spectral idempotents corresponding to the distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_r$ of $A$. The continuous-time quantum walk on $G$ is governed by the unitary $U(t)=\exp(itA)$, and its mixing matrix at time $t$ is defined by
$$M(t) = U(t)\circ \overline{U(t)},$$
where $\circ$ denotes the Schur (entrywise) product. The average mixing matrix of $G$ is
$$\hat{M} = \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T M(t)\,dt = \sum_{r=0}^{d} E_r\circ E_r.$$
A symmetric matrix $N\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is called completely positive semidefinite (cpsd) if there exist Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb{C}^{k\times k}$ (for some $k$) such that $N_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}(X_iX_j)$ for all $i,j$. The completely positive semidefinite rank (cpsd-rank) of such an $N$ is the smallest positive integer $k$ for which such a Gram representation by $k\times k$ Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices exists.

Problem: Determine the cpsd-rank of the average mixing matrix $\hat{M}$ of an arbitrary graph $G$ (or, more generally, characterize $\operatorname{cpsd\text{-}rank}(\hat{M})$ in terms of spectral or combinatorial invariants of $G$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of computing the cpsd-rank of the average mixing matrix is posed as an open problem in recent surveys and research papers on continuous-time quantum walks. A 2024 survey lists it explicitly as an unresolved question, and no subsequent work appears to provide a general formula or characterization. Some partial spectral/combinatorial bounds exist (e.g., relations to the rank of $\hat{M}$ and to graph automorphisms), but a general computation remains open.
